title: Free fall
target: Describe and calculate ideal free fall near Earth.
criteria: Use equal velocity changes in equal times.
Separate acceleration from mass and current velocity.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Which condition is required for the simple near-surface free-fall model?
options: Air resistance is negligible and gravity is approximately uniform.
cpa.guide: Free fall describes motion under gravity alone; constant g is a near-surface approximation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A feather and a metal sphere are released together in a vacuum near the surface. Which ideal prediction is correct?
options: The feather has no gravitational force.
The metal sphere must accelerate faster because it is heavier.
cpa.guide: With negligible resistance, gravitational acceleration does not depend on test mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Take downward as positive and g = 10 m/s². A ball initially moves downward at 3 m/s. What is velocity 2 s later in free fall?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: In constant-g free fall, velocity changes by 9.8 m/s in 1 s. What is the change over 0.5 s?
options: Zero because less than one second elapsed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: At the highest point of an upward toss without air resistance, which is true?
options: Vertical velocity is zero momentarily; acceleration remains downward.
Both velocity and acceleration are zero.
Gravity acts only while the ball moves downward.
cpa.guide: Zero instantaneous velocity does not imply zero acceleration.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Two falling objects have different current downward speeds in the same uniform field without resistance. Compare accelerations.
options: The slower object necessarily accelerates more.
The faster object necessarily accelerates more.
Both accelerations are zero because they already move.
cpa.guide: In this model acceleration is set by g, not current speed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
